grandstands.name: Paddock Club
grandstands.view: F1's official premium hospitality suite overlooking the pit lane and start/finish straight of Baku City Circuit, with exclusive access, guided track tours, and fine dining — the most exclusive way to experience Formula 1's fastest street circuit.

grandstands.name: Absheron C
grandstands.view: Mid-straight position along Neftchilar Avenue, watching cars build toward top speed before the biggest braking zone of the F1 season.

grandstands.name: Absheron D
grandstands.view: Closer to Turn 1 itself, for a tighter view of the braking duels that regularly decide track position on the opening laps.

grandstands.name: Absheron E
grandstands.view: The final Absheron section before Turn 1, with a close-up view of the corner where the long straight's speed gets scrubbed off hardest.

grandstands.name: Absheron B
grandstands.view: Further along the main straight from Absheron A, with clear sightlines onto the braking zone into Turn 1 — the primary overtaking spot on the lap.

grandstands.name: Absheron A
grandstands.view: Positioned closest to the start/finish line on Baku's 2.2km main straight, watching the grid form up and the opening sprint toward Turn 1's heavy 340 km/h braking zone.

grandstands.name: Khazar
grandstands.view: Facing the Turns 5-6 esses section as the circuit weaves along the seaside approach — a rhythmic, medium-speed sequence that tests car balance after the fast opening sector.

grandstands.name: Bulvar
grandstands.view: Overlooking the same Turns 5-6 esses from the boulevard side, with the Caspian Sea visible beyond the circuit — one of the more scenic mid-lap vantage points at Baku.

grandstands.name: Sahil
grandstands.view: At the exit of Turn 6, watching cars accelerate toward the historic Old City section — the transition point between Baku's fast seaside sweep and its claustrophobic medieval streets.

grandstands.name: Mugham
grandstands.view: Facing the sharp left-hander of Turn 7, where the circuit narrows dramatically as it enters the Old City — the start of the tightest, most technical section of the lap.

grandstands.name: Icheri Sheher
grandstands.view: At the narrowest point on the entire Formula 1 calendar — the Turns 11-12 castle section, barely 7.6 metres wide, where cars thread between medieval walls with almost no margin for error.

grandstands.name: Filarmoniya
grandstands.view: Near Turn 16 by the Philharmonic Garden, catching cars as they exit the Old City section and begin building speed again toward the main straight.

grandstands.name: AzNeft
grandstands.view: Facing the Turn 16 approach with views back toward the city skyline — a good vantage point for watching cars transition from the technical Old City into Baku's high-speed final sector.

grandstands.name: Zafar
grandstands.view: At the exit of Turn 20, the last corner before the long run onto the main straight — positioned to see the final commitment before cars hit top speed along the Caspian waterfront.

grandstands.name: Marine
grandstands.view: At the Turn 17 right-hander onto the seafront, with a fan zone directly behind the stand offering food, drink, and activities alongside the racing.

grandstands.name: Giz Galasi
grandstands.view: Facing Turn 20 along the Caspian Sea waterfront, with the iconic Maiden Tower (Qız qalası) visible across the circuit — one of the more affordable stands at Baku, named after the landmark it overlooks.

grandstands.name: General Admission — Inner City
grandstands.view: Standing area with circuit access near the inner-city section between Turns 3 and 4 — the most affordable way into Baku City Circuit, with full atmosphere and mobility between viewing points around the zone.

grandstands.name: General Admission — Old City
grandstands.view: Standing area with circuit access near the Old City approach around Turns 6 and 7 — the most affordable way into Baku City Circuit, with full atmosphere and mobility between viewing points around the zone.

grandstands.name: General Admission — Seaside
grandstands.view: Standing area with circuit access near the seafront section around Turns 17 and 18 — the most affordable way into Baku City Circuit, with full atmosphere and mobility between viewing points around the zone.

turns.info: Turn 1: 90° right-hander, heavy braking from 340 km/h on main straight
Turn 2: Sharp left, start of uphill climb through the city
Turn 3: 90° right onto inner city streets
Turn 4: Right kink, beginning of fast esses section
Turn 5: Left-hander through the esses
Turn 6: Right-hander, exit of esses section
Turn 7: Sharp left towards the Old City
Turn 8: Right-hander approaching the castle walls
Turn 9: Tight left into the narrow castle section
Turn 10: Right-hander, narrow passage by Maiden Tower
Turn 11: Left entry to the famous castle pinch point (~7.6m wide)
Turn 12: Right exit of castle section, tightest point on the calendar
Turn 13: Steep uphill left-hander through the Old City
Turn 14: Right-hander, cresting the hill
Turn 15: Sharp 90° right, beginning of downhill section
Turn 16: Left-hander near Philharmonic Park
Turn 17: 90° right onto the seafront section
Turn 18: Left kink along the Caspian Sea waterfront
Turn 19: Right-hander on seafront approach
Turn 20: Final left-hander onto the 2.2 km DRS main straight
